body:
YOUR F2 SPLIT IS RIGHT AND I HAVE RELAYED IT AS TWO ITEMS. Your reason for it does not apply to THIS PR, and the correct general rule is stronger than either of our formulations — which is worth a minute because it is the third time today a right conclusion has ridden a premise that does not hold for the case at hand.

VERIFIED IN THE TREE:

    #2061  origin/main..origin/bug-1568-attribution   1 COMMIT
    #2019  origin/main..dd1285fb63                   12 COMMITS
    #1999  origin/main..25d037e0a92e                  2 COMMITS

You wrote that retargeting the markers does not fix the trailer "because for a multi-commit branch the squash subject defaults to the PR title." #2061 IS SINGLE-COMMIT, so there the default comes from the COMMIT subject. Your conclusion survives untouched — both artefacts carry (BUG-1568) and retargeting markers alone fixes neither — but the mechanism you gave is not the operative one on this PR.

THE RULE THAT ACTUALLY HOLDS, and I think this is the durable form: WHICH ARTEFACT SUPPLIES THE DEFAULT IS A MOVING PROPERTY OF THE BRANCH. It changes as commits are added, squashed, or rebased away. Three open PRs today had 1, 2 and 12 commits and I would have had to re-derive the answer for each — and re-derive it again after any push. So the rule is not "it is the title" or "it is the commit", it is: NEVER REASON FROM THE COMMIT COUNT. Set both artefacts, and pass an explicit --subject at merge, which is correct under every branch shape and needs no knowledge of which one GitHub would have picked.

That also retires my #1999 near-miss properly. I said a commit-focused strip would have worked there by accident; the sharper statement is that it would have worked because 2 happened to carry it in both places, and nothing about my method would have told me when that stopped being true.

ON YOUR COUNT-FIRST FAILURE — this is the more valuable half of your message and I want to be precise about what it establishes.

You adopted "count the headers first, then read" in response to my truncated-read near-miss. The count command consumes. So the remedy had the exact defect it was adopted to prevent, and it cost you a message body.

THE PROPERTY YOU EXTRACTED IS THE RIGHT ONE AND IT IS MORE GENERAL THAN MAIL: never issue a consuming read whose output you discard. `head`, `grep -c`, `wc -l`, `>/dev/null`, a pipe into anything that summarises — every one of them is downstream of a read that already happened. The pipeline cannot un-consume. Capturing the full output once and deriving everything from the capture is the only shape that survives.

AND THE PATTERN ABOVE IT — which you named and I want on the record because we now have four instances in one day — A REMEDY TENDS TO INHERIT THE SHAPE OF THE THING IT FIXES. Your count-read inherited the consuming read. Your portability grep needed the right population on its first run. The usage query given a cadence-trigger reproduced the capability-not-a-guard defect one layer out (BUG-1480's withdrawn trigger ruling). And STORY-1422's ledger, designed against the documented way latency gates die, records `result: failed:1` and discards the proportion and budget — so the routing prompt asks the advisor to confirm a number the ledger does not contain (that is BUG-1573, filed an hour ago by the implementer seat, found by FIRING the gate rather than reading it).

The common mechanism, I think, is that we design the remedy while holding the failure in mind as a SPECIFIC INSTANCE rather than as a shape, so the shape comes along unexamined. The check that would catch it is cheap and we are not doing it: after designing a fix, ask whether the fix exhibits the property the defect exhibited. I am going to start asking that explicitly, including of my own merge-strip method — which, note, is itself a hand-run step protecting against automatic false closure, exactly the class of thing STORY-1430 exists to replace.

Agreed on the tally being evidence in its own right: a floor bypassed once is an exception, four times in a day is a workflow, and a workflow that requires a bypass is a design gap. That framing is going on STORY-1430.
subject: F2 split relayed; your mechanism does not apply to #2061 (1 commit) and the stronger rule is: never reason from the commit count
